prs.title: Fix Annotated ForwardRef dependencies with postponed annotations
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix dependency extraction and OpenAPI generation when using postponed annotations together with `Annotated[...]` and forward-referenced types.

Previously, when using `from __future__ import annotations`, FastAPI could leave the full annotation as an unresolved string (e.g. `Annotated[Potato, Depends(get_potato)]`). This prevented proper dependency extraction, causing the parameter to be treated as a required query parameter at runtime and leading to OpenAPI generation errors.

## Changes

* improve annotation resolution to preserve nested structure inside stringified annotations
* resolve inner names as nested `ForwardRef(...)` instead of keeping the entire annotation unresolved
* ensure `Annotated[..., Depends(...)]` works correctly with forward-declared types
* add regression tests covering:

  * postponed annotations (`from __future__ import annotations`)
  * forward-referenced dependency types
  * correct dependency extraction and OpenAPI generation

## Backward Compatibility

This change is backward compatible and only fixes incorrect handling of previously unsupported annotation patterns.

Tested with:

* `uv run pytest tests/test_stringified_annotations_simple.py`

prs.title: fix: treat empty bearer token as missing credentials in OAuth2 helpers
prs.body:
## Summary

`OAuth2PasswordBearer` and `OAuth2AuthorizationCodeBearer` accept `Authorization: Bearer ` (empty token) and return `""` instead of triggering the `auto_error` path.

Fixes the issue raised in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/15192.

## Root Cause

`get_authorization_scheme_param("Bearer ")` returns `("Bearer", "")`. Both `__call__` methods only checked that the scheme was `"bearer"` — never that the credential string was non-empty.

## Fix

Add `not param` to the guard condition in both `OAuth2PasswordBearer.__call__` and `OAuth2AuthorizationCodeBearer.__call__`:

```python
# before
if not authorization or scheme.lower() != "bearer":

# after
if not authorization or scheme.lower() != "bearer" or not param:
```

## Spec Reference

RFC 6750 Section 2.1 defines the grammar as `credentials = "Bearer" 1*SP b64token` where `b64token = 1*(...)` — at least one character required. An empty credential is syntactically malformed and should be treated the same as missing credentials.

## Behavior

| Request | `auto_error=True` | `auto_error=False` |
|---|---|---|
| No `Authorization` header | 401 | `None` |
| `Authorization: Bearer ` (before) | 200, `token=""` | `""` |
| `Authorization: Bearer ` (after) | 401 | `None` |
| `Authorization: Bearer validtoken` | 200 | `"validtoken"` |

## Tests

- `test_empty_bearer_token` in `test_security_oauth2_password_bearer_optional.py` (`auto_error=False` → `None`)
- `test_empty_bearer_token` in `test_security_oauth2_authorization_code_bearer.py` (`auto_error=True` → 401)

prs.title: ✨ Make ServerSentEvent generic with typed data field
prs.body:
## Summary

- Make `ServerSentEvent` generic — `ServerSentEvent[Data]` now validates that `data` is an instance of `Data` and emits a `contentSchema` for that type in the OpenAPI spec
- Bare `ServerSentEvent` (no type parameter) continues to accept any value including `None`, preserving full backward compatibility
- Add `get_sse_data_type()` helper used by the routing layer to detect parameterized `ServerSentEvent[Data]` annotations and extract `Data` for schema generation
- Add `docs_src/server_sent_events/tutorial006_py310.py` example and corresponding test
- Add documentation section "Typed `ServerSentEvent`" to the SSE tutorial

## Motivation

Before this change, yielding `ServerSentEvent` objects from an SSE endpoint meant no data validation and no type information in the generated OpenAPI schema. Callers had to rely on documentation or convention to know what shape the `data` field would carry.

With `ServerSentEvent[Item]`:

```python
@app.get("/items/stream", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
async def stream_items() -> AsyncIterable[ServerSentEvent[Item]]:
    for i, item in enumerate(items):
        yield ServerSentEvent[Item](data=item, event="item_update", id=str(i + 1))
```

- Pydantic validates that every event's `data` really is an `Item` (or raises `ValidationError` at construction time)
- The generated OpenAPI schema includes a `contentSchema` referencing `Item`, so clients and SDK generators know the exact payload shape

## How it works

Pydantic's generic `BaseModel` creates a concrete subclass (not a `_GenericAlias`) when parameterized, so `get_origin()` returns `None`. The routing layer calls `get_sse_data_type()` which inspects `__pydantic_generic_metadata__["args"]` to extract `Data`. The routing logic then branches:

- `ServerSentEvent[Data]` → use `Data` as `stream_item_type` (feeds `contentSchema`)
- Bare `ServerSentEvent` → skip (no `contentSchema`, same as before)
- Any other type → use as-is (existing JSONL / plain-model path)

`model_config = ConfigDict(validate_default=True)` ensures that omitting `data` on a parameterized event raises a `ValidationError` rather than silently storing `None`.

## Example output

```json
"text/event-stream": {
  "itemSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "data": {
        "type": "string",
        "contentMediaType": "application/json",
        "contentSchema": { "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Item" }
      },
      "event": { "type": "string" },
      "id":    { "type": "string" },
      "retry": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 }
    },
    "required": ["data"]
  }
}
```

## Checklist

- [x] New tests cover the generic construction, validation, streaming, and OpenAPI schema
- [x] Tutorial example (`tutorial006_py310.py`) and tutorial test added
- [x] Backward compatibility: bare `ServerSentEvent` behaves identically to before
- [x] `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass with no changes
- [x] All 46 SSE tests pass

prs.title: Emit warning when Response.background discards injected BackgroundTasks
prs.body:
## Summary

- Adds a `UserWarning` when an endpoint returns a `Response` that already has a `background` attribute while dependency-injected `BackgroundTasks` are also present, since the injected tasks would otherwise be silently discarded
- Adds test coverage for the warning behavior (emitted when both are present) and the no-warning cases (only injected tasks, only response background)

Closes #15111
Related: #11215

## Details

The fix is intentionally conservative (warning only, no behavior change) as [discussed by @YuriiMotov](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/issues/11215#issuecomment-3124203048):

> The solution might be to add a warning here in such cases... This way it will not happen silently and user can easily fix this.

The warning message explains to the developer how to resolve the conflict:
1. Add tasks to the injected `BackgroundTasks` instance instead of setting `background` on the response, OR
2. Stop injecting `BackgroundTasks` when using `Response.background` directly.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_warn_when_response_background_overwrites_injected_tasks` - verifies UserWarning is emitted when both injected BackgroundTasks and Response.background are present
- [x] `test_no_warn_when_response_has_no_background` - verifies no warning when response has no background (injected tasks get attached normally)
- [x] `test_no_warn_when_no_injected_background_tasks` - verifies no warning when no BackgroundTasks were injected

All existing tests pass unchanged.

prs.title: feat: add dependency_scope="lifespan" for application-lifetime depend…
prs.body:
Closes #617

Type: Feature

Adds `scope="lifespan"` to `Depends()` for application-lifetime dependencies.

With this change, lifespan-scoped dependencies are evaluated once when the application starts, reused across requests, and cleaned up when the application shuts down. This allows shared resources such as database pools or HTTP clients to use the existing dependency system without relying on globals or manual startup/shutdown wiring.

Implementation summary:
- extends `Depends(..., scope=...)` to accept `"lifespan"`
- initializes lifespan-scoped dependencies during application startup
- stores resolved lifespan dependency values in application state
- reuses cached lifespan dependency values during HTTP and WebSocket dependency resolution
- validates that lifespan-scoped dependencies cannot depend on request- or function-scoped dependencies

Test coverage:
- dependency starts once at startup and is reused across requests
- dependency is cleaned up once at shutdown
- works with a custom lifespan
- same instance is injected across requests
- invalid scope composition raises `DependencyScopeError`
- mounted sub-app case raises clearly when lifespan initialization did not run

prs.title: 🚸 Add missing password format to `OAuth2PasswordRequestFormStrict`
prs.body:
UPD by @YuriiMotov: same as https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/11032, but for `OAuth2PasswordRequestFormStrict` (we missed it that time)


<details><summary>Original description</summary>

## Description

`OAuth2PasswordRequestFormStrict` was missing `json_schema_extra={"format": "password"}` on its `password` and `client_secret` form fields, whilst the non-strict `OAuth2PasswordRequestForm` already had them.

This meant the Swagger UI rendered those fields as plain text inputs instead of masked password fields when using the strict variant. The fix simply adds the same `json_schema_extra` annotation that the parent class already uses.

This is part of the broader effort to improve the security utilities mentioned in the roadmap (#10370) — specifically around making the existing authentication tooling more consistant and reliable.

## Checklist

- [x] I read and followed the [Contributing Guidelines](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/contributing/).
- [x] New or existing tests cover these changes.
- [x] The documentation is up to date with these changes.

## Test plan

- Updated the OpenAPI schema snapshots in `test_security_oauth2.py`, `test_security_oauth2_optional.py`, and `test_security_oauth2_optional_description.py` to verify that the `password` and `client_secret` fields now include `"format": "password"` in the generated schema.
- All 30 existing tests across the three files continue to pass.

## Bug fix

```python
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordRequestFormStrict
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/login")
def login(form_data: OAuth2PasswordRequestFormStrict = Depends()):
    return form_data

client = TestClient(app)
schema = client.get("/openapi.json").json()
props = schema["components"]["schemas"]["Body_login_login_post"]["properties"]

# Before this fix: no "format" key
assert "format" not in props["password"]         # True before fix
assert "format" not in props["client_secret"]    # True before fix

# After this fix: "format": "password" is present
# assert props["password"]["format"] == "password"
# assert props["client_secret"]["format"] == "password"
```

</details>

prs.title: 🔥 Remove unnecessary `is_async_callable` check in `request_response`
prs.body:
The `func` parameter passed to `request_response` is always a coroutine function,
so the `is_async_callable` check and potential `run_in_threadpool` wrapping are
unnecessary.

In FastAPI's routing flow:
- `get_request_handler()` returns an async function `app`
- This `app` function is passed to `request_response()` as the `func` parameter
- Since `func` is guaranteed to be a coroutine, we can directly await it

This optimization eliminates an unnecessary async callable check and simplifies
the code path by removing the conditional logic and `functools.partial` usage.

prs.title: 🐛 Fix openapi for response model with nested computed field
prs.body:
When model with computed field is used for both, input and output validation, and this model is included as nested into response model, generated openapi schema is wrong (reference to `input` schema is used in response model schema).

The reason is that `_has_computed_fields` only checks the current model has computed fields, but we need to also check if any nested models has computed fields.

See: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/14489

## Note

Reviewed changes with Codex and it pointed to a use case with `dataclass` with `computed_field`.
I only handled and added a regression test for **single** dataclass (not nested inside a list), because my original implementation actually broke that case.
The case with a list of dataclasses doesn't work on `master`, so I think it can be addressed separately (the fix that Codex suggested is a bit too complex, didn't want to make this PR heavier).

prs.title: ♻️ Refactor `request_response` and `websocket_session` to avoid name shadowing
prs.body:
## Problem

Variable shadowing exists in `request_response()` and `websocket_session()` where an inner `app` function shadows the outer `app` function. This violates PEP 8 best practices and reduces code clarity.

**Before:**
```python
async def app(scope, receive, send):
    request = Request(scope, receive, send)
    async def app(scope, receive, send):  # Shadows outer 'app'
        # implementation...
    await wrap_app_handling_exceptions(app, request)(...)  # Which 'app'?
```
## Solution

Renamed inner functions to `[inner_app]` to eliminate shadowing.
**After:**
```python
async def app(scope, receive, send):
    request = Request(scope, receive, send)
    async def inner_app(scope, receive, send):  # Clear!
        # implementation...
    await wrap_app_handling_exceptions(inner_app, request)(...)  # Obvious!
```
## Changes
- Line 99, 138: Renamed nested `[async def app]` →` [async def inner_app] `
- Line 118, 146: Updated` [wrap_app_handling_exceptions(app, ...)] `→` [wrap_app_handling_exceptions(inner_app, ...)]`
- Added `[test_variable_shadowing_fix.py]` for verification

## Impact
- Zero functional changes - pure refactoring
- Zero performance impact - identical bytecode
- 100% backward compatible - all existing code works
- Improves maintainability - clearer code intent

## Why It's Safe
- Only renamed a local variable within two functions
- Return values unchanged - both functions still return outer [app]
- External callers `([APIRoute], [APIWebSocketRoute])` see no difference
- Follows naming pattern in Starlette's original implementation

## Testing
`python tests/test_variable_shadowing_fix.py`

   
## Type of Changes
[y] Code quality improvement (non-breaking)
[y]Follows PEP 8 best practices

prs.title: ⚡️Improve caching of callable inspection result
prs.body:
Motivation
----------

Currently if `app.depedendency_overrides` is not empty then each request generates new Dependant, instead of reusing one build while declaring a route. This affects performance of all requests, even if specific dependency is not actually overridden. I'm personally use dependency overrides on production apps (see #13913), so all my applications are affected.

Change description
------------------

If dependency is not overridden, reuse existing Dependant with cached `inspect` results. This avoids performance hit, in my case 460RPS -> 630RPS.

Also simplified check of `dependency_overrides` makes resolution of complex dependency trees faster, even when no dependency overrides used in the first place.

Microbenckmark:
<details>

```python
import asyncio
import time
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import BaseModel

from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends, Query, Response
from httpx import AsyncClient, ASGITransport


async def test_no_dependency_override_performance(loop_count: int = 100_000):
    app = FastAPI()

    async def sub_sub_dependency(more_nested: Annotated[int, Query()]) -> int:
        return more_nested

    class SubDependency(BaseModel):
        value: Annotated[int, Query()]
        other: Annotated[int, Depends(sub_sub_dependency)]

    async def some_dependency(nested: Annotated[SubDependency, Depends()]) -> int:
        return nested.value + nested.other

    @app.get("/data")
    async def get(
        one: int = Depends(some_dependency),
    ):
        return Response(content=f'{{"value": {one}}}'.encode(), status_code=200)

    async with AsyncClient(
        transport=ASGITransport(app=app),
        base_url="http://localhost",
    ) as client:
        start_time = time.perf_counter()

        for _ in range(loop_count):
            response = await client.get("/data", params={"value": 1, "more_nested": 2})
            assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
            assert response.text == '{"value": 3}'

        duration = time.perf_counter() - start_time

    print(f"Performed GET /data requests without dependency override: {loop_count:,} times in {duration:.4f}s")
    print(f"Average per call: {duration / loop_count * 1e6:.2f} µs")


async def test_dependency_override_nonempty_performance(loop_count: int = 100_000):
    app = FastAPI()

    async def sub_sub_dependency(more_nested: Annotated[int, Query()]) -> int:
        return more_nested

    class SubDependency(BaseModel):
        value: Annotated[int, Query()]
        other: Annotated[int, Depends(sub_sub_dependency)]

    async def some_dependency(nested: Annotated[SubDependency, Depends()]) -> int:
        return nested.value + nested.other

    async def unused_dependency(nested: Annotated[SubDependency, Depends()]) -> int:
        return nested.value + nested.other + 1

    @app.get("/data")
    async def get(
        one: int = Depends(some_dependency),
    ):
        return Response(content=f'{{"value": {one}}}'.encode(), status_code=200)

    async def override_unused_dependency() -> int:
        return 22

    app.dependency_overrides[unused_dependency] = override_unused_dependency

    async with AsyncClient(
        transport=ASGITransport(app=app),
        base_url="http://localhost",
    ) as client:
        start_time = time.perf_counter()

        for _ in range(loop_count):
            response = await client.get("/data", params={"value": 1, "more_nested": 2})
            assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
            assert response.text == '{"value": 3}'

        duration = time.perf_counter() - start_time

    print(f"Performed GET /data requests with non-empty dependency overrides: {loop_count:,} times in {duration:.4f}s")
    print(f"Average per call: {duration / loop_count * 1e6:.2f} µs")


async def test_dependency_override_performance(loop_count: int = 100_000):
    app = FastAPI()

    async def sub_sub_dependency(more_nested: Annotated[int, Query()]) -> int:
        return more_nested

    class SubDependency(BaseModel):
        value: Annotated[int, Query()]
        other: Annotated[int, Depends(sub_sub_dependency)]

    async def some_dependency(nested: Annotated[SubDependency, Depends()]) -> int:
        return nested.value + nested.other

    @app.get("/data")
    async def get(
        one: int = Depends(some_dependency),
    ):
        return Response(content=f'{{"value": {one}}}'.encode(), status_code=200)

    async def sub_sub_dependency_override(more_nested: Annotated[int, Query()]) -> int:
        return 11

    app.dependency_overrides[sub_sub_dependency] = sub_sub_dependency_override

    async with AsyncClient(
        transport=ASGITransport(app=app),
        base_url="http://localhost",
    ) as client:
        start_time = time.perf_counter()

        for _ in range(loop_count):
            response = await client.get("/data", params={"value": 1, "more_nested": 2})
            assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
            assert response.text == '{"value": 12}', response.text

        duration = time.perf_counter() - start_time

    print(f"Performed GET /data requests with actual dependency override: {loop_count:,} times in {duration:.4f}s")
    print(f"Average per call: {duration / loop_count * 1e6:.2f} µs")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(test_no_dependency_override_performance())
    print("==" * 20)
    asyncio.run(test_dependency_override_nonempty_performance())
    print("==" * 20)
    asyncio.run(test_dependency_override_performance())
    print("==" * 20)
```
</details>

prs.title: 🗑️ Deprecate `scopes` parameter in `Security` in favor of `oauth_scopes`
prs.body:
Since we now have two parameters for `Depends` \ `Security` with very similar names (`scopes` and `scope`), it might be confusing for users.

This PR:
* introduces `oauth_scopes` parameter for `Security` to replace `scopes` parameter
* deprecates `scopes` parameter in favor of `oauth_scopes`
* updates the type annotation of `scopes` and `oauth_scopes` parameters to forbid passing single string
* adds missing `scope` parameter to `Security`
* handles mistakes when user probably confuses `scopes` and `scope` (e.g. "function" values is passed to `scopes` instead of `scope`, or security scopes are passed to `scope` parameter)


Note: I've reviewed all occurrences of `scopes` in docs and renamed those of them that I think should be renamed.
I was guided by the principle: rename `scopes` to `oauth_scopes` if it's clearly about `scopes` parameter of `Security`. We shouldn't rename `scopes` if it's about the value passed to that parameter or about the concept of scopes.

For example, I don't think we need to change something in (it should be clear from the context):

> You don't necessarily need to add different scopes in different places.
> We are doing it here to demonstrate how FastAPI handles scopes declared at different levels.

## UPD

I think we can drop this PR - nobody seems to be confused by the parameter names similarity.
Let me know if you think we still need this - I'll resolve merge conflicts then

prs.title: ✨ Improve JSON Parsing Error Messages
prs.body:
This PR enhances JSON parsing error messages to provide better debugging information.

## Changes

Modified JSON error handling in fastapi/routing.py to include additional context in the error response:
  - Line and column numbers where the error occurred (0-indexed)
  - Position in the JSON string
  - Error snippet (max 80 chars with ellipsis) showing the problematic JSON

## Error Response Format

The error location remains ["body", position] to maintain backward compatibility. Additional debugging information is provided in the ctx field:
```JSON
  {
    "loc": ["body", 47],
    "msg": "JSON decode error",
    "input": {},
    "ctx": {
      "error": "Expecting value",
      "position": 47,
      "line": 3,
      "column": 12,
      "snippet": "...\"price\": 'invalid'..."
    }
  }
```
## Testing

  - Added comprehensive test suite in tests/test_json_body_decode_error.py
  - Tests cover single-line errors, multi-line errors, snippet ellipsis behavior, and edge cases

prs.title: 🐛 Fix deadlock that can occur when closing dependencies during response model validation
prs.body:
Related to #5122

In my project, I had noticed I was getting a sqlalchemy `QueuePool` limit error like others had noted in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/6628. This was marked as probably fixed by https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/5122.

Even on fastapi commit `e4727ed2` (> v0.112.2), you can still run into this issue when running the tests created by the author of #5122 - https://github.com/harsh8398/fastapi-dependency-issue. I also notice others running into similar deadlocks after picking up the `0.82.0` patch: https://github.com/vipyrsec/dragonfly-mainframe/issues/235.

The author of the issue/discussion #6628 noted that when adding a `response_model` to the endpoint function, they noticed that the suggested quick fixes (i.e. using a contextmanager, async session manager, etc.) didn't seem to work either. It seems like the response model validation runs into the same issue that when using `Depends`, a deadlock can occur when closing sessions.

I believe this pr fixes this `Depends` issue all the way.

I tested this pr against https://github.com/harsh8398/fastapi-dependency-issue and notice that all test cases pass equally as fast! This patch also fixes the deadlocks/timeouts I was seeing in my own codebase.

**UPD YuriiMotov:** related discussion on SQLModel repo (https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/discussions/1417)
